correctness.rationale: For distinct centers at distances one, two and at least three, closed-ball intersections are respectively a coordinate line, two recombinations and empty. On a coordinate line any ball restricts to the full line, one center or none. Four static queries would force their four triple-positive subsets into a single line, contradicting the required two-positive trace. Every first-positive adaptive version space is one ball and cannot shatter depth three, giving Ldim<=3. H(3,2) and H(2,4) provide three-query static seeds; H(2,3) has VC=2 by the row-column corner obstruction and Ldim=3 by the explicit depth-three tree. Degenerate cases follow directly. The embedded finite checker verified nine parameter examples and all eight tree paths; its enumeration is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The earliest motivating primary paper is arXiv:2007.16042 (2020-07-31). Its Hamming section is about open neighborhoods, and the paper gives only general boundedness for closed ones. Exact closed neighborhoods and the static/adaptive parameter gap are a different claim; at H(3,2) the open and closed static dimensions disagree. A later 2025 paper also treats open-neighborhood VC on induced subsets; general thicket theory supplies definitions, not these formulas. Available semantic-record and local-claim comparison did not find dominating coverage. Residual priority risk remains.

value.rationale: A natural two-parameter family of distance-transitive graphs receives a complete exact classification of both static and adaptive shattering, including the sole strict gap. The proof isolates a reusable coordinate-line intersection obstruction, establishes the optimal realizable online mistake budget and gives a universal hereditary upper bound. This exact infinite-family answer is more than a small numerical improvement, and the open/closed contrast at H(3,2) is structurally informative.
